**Finding submitted: deviation (critical) at § 14.2 (p0054).**

- **Issue:** Vendor takes exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created for us, with only a *revocable, non-transferable, term-limited* licence back. That misses the preferred position (we own what we pay for, Vendor assigns) and also fails the fallback, which requires a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable licence to use and modify Deliverables.
- **Why 13.2/14.3 don't cure it:** the perpetual licence reaches only Vendor Technology embedded in or required to use a Deliverable — not the Deliverable itself — and 13.3 expressly contemplates revocation.
- **Compliant neighbours (not flagged):** 14.1 (Customer owns Customer Data and pre-existing IP), 14.3 (Vendor retains Vendor Technology — acceptable), 14.4 (no joint ownership; feedback rights preserved).
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** flips 14.2 to Customer ownership with an irrevocable assignment on creation, while preserving Vendor's retention of Vendor Technology under 14.3; the comment offers the licence-back fallback as an alternative.
